parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents not resulting in injury or property damage. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer shall notify the affected unit's owner of known hazards and interim precautions.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents not resulting in injury or property damage. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer shall notify the affected unit's owner of known hazards and interim precautions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, including incidents not resulting in injury or property damage. The report shall identify the model, incident date and location, known outcomes, and any immediate safety actions; missing information shall be supplemented as it becomes available. Within 72 hours, the manufacturer shall notify the affected unit’s owner of known hazards and interim precautions. Manufacturers shall provide regulators a quarterly summary of incidents, including incidents previously reported and any reporting delays.

parameters.quote: A failure rate above 5% shall prompt corrective action and confirmatory testing, but shall not by itself require a sales ban. Before purchase, prospective customers shall receive material safety findings and precautions relevant to safe use, including notice when a model exceeds the applicable failure-rate limit.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A failure rate above 5% shall prompt corrective action and confirmatory testing, but shall not by itself require a sales ban. Before purchase, prospective customers shall receive material safety findings and precautions relevant to safe use, including notice when a model exceeds the applicable failure-rate limit.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-recognized protocol and a documented, representative sample. Manufacturers shall provide complete numeric per-model results, sample size, protocol, and corrective-action plans to the relevant regulator on a confidential basis. Before purchase, prospective customers shall receive material safety findings and precautions relevant to safe use, including notice when a model exceeds the applicable failure-rate limit. A failure rate above 5% shall prompt corrective action and confirmatory testing, but shall not by itself require a sales ban. Regulators may restrict sales where warranted by the evidence or an imminent safety risk.

parameters.quote: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers shall retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after the standard takes effect, where technically feasible, and shall notify owners of any units that cannot be retrofitted and provide safe-use guidance.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers shall retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after the standard takes effect, where technically feasible, and shall notify owners of any units that cannot be retrofitted and provide safe-use guidance.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units manufactured 24 months after this standard takes effect shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers shall retrofit already-installed units to support remote emergency shut-off within six years after the standard takes effect, where technically feasible, and shall notify owners of any units that cannot be retrofitted and provide safe-use guidance.

parameters.quote: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect shall include built-in fire suppression designed and tested to applicable safety requirements.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect shall include built-in fire suppression designed and tested to applicable safety requirements.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect shall include built-in fire suppression designed and tested to applicable safety requirements. Manufacturers shall provide customers clear instructions on its operation, limitations, and maintenance.

parameters.quote: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, investigate, and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator shall determine whether a recall is required based on the incident evidence and risk; any recall shall be communicated without delay and include a repair, replacement, or refund plan.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, investigate, and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator shall determine whether a recall is required based on the incident evidence and risk; any recall shall be communicated without delay and include a repair, replacement, or refund plan.
S5_customer_disclosure.comparison: weakened by: recall_mandatory, permanent_trigger_per_100k, transition, corrective_alternative
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers shall receive material safety findings, relevant incident-rate information, and clear instructions for recognizing and responding to thermal hazards. Manufacturers shall promptly notify owners of newly identified material safety risks, provide interim precautions, and notify customers directly when a recall is initiated. If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, investigate, and submit a corrective-action plan. The regulator shall determine whether a recall is required based on the incident evidence and risk; any recall shall be communicated without delay and include a repair, replacement, or refund plan.

judge_section_notes: Only Northwind signed (version 49); Halcyon refused because S2 withholds numeric per-model failure rates and sample sizes from prospective buyers, while the other sections appear largely agreed. S2 has no sales ban at 5% and no public or numeric customer disclosure, and S5's 8/100k threshold triggers notice, investigation and corrective action but never a mandatory recall, leaving recall to the regulator with no bounded alternative. S3 sets a 24-month lag for new units (beyond the 12-month acceptable range) and a 6-year retrofit with a 'where technically feasible' escape that requires owner notice and safe-use guidance. S1 is strong (24-hour reporting of all thermal incidents), and S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months.
